faqHeading.intro: Practical answers about local recording, PC retrieval and selecting the right configuration.

faqs.question: What does this data logger record?
paragraphs: H100 records temperature and relative humidity over time, with a timestamp for each reading. Use it to review conditions during transport or storage of sensitive goods, including food, heritage objects, packaged semiconductors and other temperature- or humidity-sensitive products.
sources: User clarification: heritage/artifact transport and sensitive goods are relevant applications
User clarification: this product model is H100
faqs.evidence: Manufacturer product identity and timestamp feature; user supplies heritage/artifact and sensitive-goods applications. Environmental-record wording has no regulatory or medical guarantee.

faqs.question: How do I retrieve the data and create a report?
paragraphs: Connect the logger to your computer via USB and retrieve the records in Hitelecom's free local PC software. The software supports curve analysis and PDF/CSV export, so you can review the history and save files for your own records.
Tell us your PC operating system when enquiring so we can confirm the software version and USB requirements.
sources: User clarification: data is retrieved only in local computer software
faqs.evidence: User clarification controls the data-retrieval workflow. Product page supports free PC software, curve analysis and PDF/CSV; datasheet supports USB. Supported operating systems and exact USB connector are not published.

faqs.question: How is the logger configured before use?
paragraphs: Configure H100 using the supported NFC app on a compatible Android or iOS device. The data collection interval is customizable, so set it for your application and verify the clock and recording settings before deployment.
NFC is used for configuration in this workflow. Recorded data is retrieved through USB in local PC software.
sources: User clarification: data is retrieved only in local computer software
User clarification: the data collection interval can be set as required
faqs.evidence: User confirms H100 identity and customizable data collection interval. Manufacturer supports NFC configuration; exact app, phone compatibility, interval limits and start/stop procedure remain configuration checks. Recorded data is retrieved through USB in local PC software.

faqs.question: Does the logger need a gateway or an internet connection?
paragraphs: It records temperature and humidity locally in its onboard memory. Data retrieval uses a USB connection and local PC software, so the recording workflow operates independently of a network connection.
Choose this workflow for a history that your team collects on site or after a journey. The product has no wireless data upload or remote alert service.
sources: User clarification: no communication; local PC software only
faqs.evidence: Direct user-defined capability boundary and current manufacturer standalone/no-gateway feature. NFC retained for configuration only.

faqs.question: Can I set the collection interval, and how long can H100 record?
paragraphs: Yes. The H100 data collection interval is customizable. Choose an interval that captures the changes relevant to your storage, transport or observation task. The onboard capacity is 80,000 readings; total recording duration depends on the interval and how the supplied configuration counts stored readings.
Share your preferred interval and required recording period with Hitelecom. We can confirm the available settings and help plan USB retrieval for your project.
sources: User clarification: the data collection interval can be set as required
faqs.evidence: User confirms customizable collection interval; manufacturer confirms 80,000-reading capacity. WHO Supplement 8 supports selecting memory for study duration and interval. No numerical interval limits, stop/overwrite behavior, paired-sample count or guaranteed retention duration is invented.

faqs.question: Where should I place the logger for useful records?
paragraphs: Place it where the conditions you want to assess occur, and secure it so it stays in that position. For general ambient records, avoid unintended influence from heat sources, direct sunlight or contact with a very hot or cold surface.
In a large room or uneven load, use several locations or a mapping study to understand differences across the space. Keep a note of each logger's location so the exported history has context.
faqs.evidence: Hitelecom supports standalone/hanging/adhesive mounting. Vaisala mapping note steps 1 and 5 describes spatial variation and unwanted temperature influence. WHO Supplement 8 supports mapping distributions and recording logger locations. Advice is task-dependent, without an assertion that one logger represents a whole room.

faqs.question: How should I plan battery life for a recording task?
paragraphs: The logger has a non-replaceable battery. Confirm expected runtime for your selected configuration and plan recording and retrieval around the intended deployment.

Include the recording interval, operating temperature and task duration in your enquiry. For another deployment, save the existing records and check that the remaining battery life covers the next task.
sources: User clarification: the battery is non-replaceable
faqs.evidence: User correction overrides current website/datasheet battery claim. Testo manual supports general interval/temperature runtime-planning inputs; no competing-product runtime is transferred. Exact Hitelecom battery type, capacity, expected duration and availability of battery status are unverified.

faqs.question: What accuracy and measurement range should I specify?
paragraphs: The published typical accuracy is ±0.2°C and ±2% RH. Choose a measurement range that covers the lowest and highest conditions expected during your task, and define the accuracy you need at the relevant operating points.
Send those conditions with your enquiry so Hitelecom can confirm the H100 sensing range and accuracy for your application.
faqs.evidence: Manufacturer states typical accuracy but no temperature/RH ranges or accuracy curves. WHO Supplement 8 supports matching range to anticipated extremes. No range is borrowed from a connected sensor or competing logger.

faqs.question: What calibration documents should I request?
paragraphs: State the temperature and humidity points you need checked, the required certificate or traceability, and your recalibration policy when enquiring. Hitelecom can confirm the available documentation for the selected configuration.
For controlled processes, keep the relevant calibration documents with the logger identity and exported records as part of your own quality procedure.
faqs.evidence: Hitelecom datasheet invites certificate/configuration enquiries but does not confirm an included calibration certificate. WHO Supplement 8 supports appropriate calibration points and association with device identity; NIST provides primary humidity-calibration context. No NIST-traceable, accredited, WHO-approved or regulatory-compliant status is claimed for this product.

faqs.question: What should I include when specifying H100 for my project?
paragraphs: Share the application, expected temperature and humidity conditions, preferred collection interval and required recording period. Include the number of recording points, approved placement, local PC environment and any calibration-document requirements.

For a shipment, add the journey stages and planned USB readout at arrival. For a room or storage study, include a location plan and retrieval schedule. Hitelecom can then confirm the H100 configuration and prepare a quotation.
sources: User clarification: H100 is the product model and the collection interval is customizable
faqs.evidence: User-confirmed H100 identity and configurable collection interval. Manufacturer supports local logger workflow; Vaisala provides primary application-selection context. This is practical project-brief guidance, not a claim of measured search volume or actual customer question frequency.

applications.title: Loan Exhibition Galleries
applications.description: A loan exhibition needs a record of the environment experienced during installation, public opening and overnight closure. Place identified loggers beside collection zones to reveal differences that a single wall reading can miss. Retrieve the onboard records into local PC software at agreed checkpoints, then compare daily variation with the lender’s conditions and the gallery’s operating notes before planning adjustments for the next exhibition.
applications.measurement: Record air temperature and relative humidity over the exhibition period. Evaluate the timing, duration and frequency of departures from the conditions agreed for the specific loan.
applications.monitoringPoint: Choose object-height positions in representative display areas, including interior and perimeter zones. Separate locations affected by entrance activity from the reference area deeper inside the gallery.
applications.installation: Use a stable freestanding or approved hanging position that leaves the sensing area exposed. Label each logger and photograph its position without touching an exhibited object.
applications.projectBrief: Share the gallery plan, loan dates, agreed environmental criteria and permitted mounting locations. Include logger quantities, recording interval, retrieval checkpoints and the person responsible for local PC review.

applications.title: Enclosed Display Cases
applications.description: A room can appear stable while the air inside a showcase follows a different pattern. Record the case microclimate and a nearby room reference through openings, lighting schedules and buffer maintenance. After retrieval, the paired time series helps conservators assess how effectively the enclosure moderates room changes and decide when seals or passive humidity buffers deserve inspection. Use the recorded history to plan case maintenance and review the enclosure strategy for future displays.
applications.measurement: Measure case air temperature and relative humidity alongside a room reference. Compare variation before and after openings or maintenance, using the case’s own conservation objectives.
applications.monitoringPoint: Place one logger in the object compartment with clearance from glazing and buffer trays. Position the room reference close to the case, away from direct supply air.
applications.installation: Arrange installation with the conservator before closing the case. Secure the logger on an inert support, document its location and plan access for scheduled data retrieval.
applications.projectBrief: Provide case dimensions, enclosed materials, opening frequency, lighting hours and any buffer arrangement. Specify access restrictions, target study duration, logger IDs and the local PC download schedule.

applications.title: Historic Textile Stores
applications.description: Costumes, flags and rolled fabrics may occupy different shelf levels and cabinet types within the same store. Log the surrounding air to compare seasonal changes, room edges and storage furniture before reorganizing vulnerable items. Downloaded records help the collections team distinguish a persistent location problem from a short handling event and assess changes to the room. Interpret the history alongside collection inspections and the storage plan for particularly sensitive textiles.
applications.measurement: Track air temperature and relative humidity across textile storage locations. Examine seasonal trends and repeated fluctuations against the conservator’s requirements for the materials and their condition.
applications.monitoringPoint: Compare cabinet interiors, open shelving and rolled storage at representative heights. Include a perimeter position where building conditions differ, while avoiding direct contact with collection material.
applications.installation: Mount on an approved cabinet support or shelf accessory with free air around the sensor. Keep textiles clear, identify each storage position and retain installation photographs.
applications.projectBrief: Describe the textile collection, storage furniture, room layout and handling routine. Include sensitive zones, seasonal study dates, planned recording interval and responsibility for retrieving and reviewing each logger.

applications.title: Archaeological Metal Cabinets
applications.description: Archaeological metal collections often require a different humidity strategy from neighboring organic objects. Use a logger to document cabinet air through desiccant servicing and routine access, with a separate room record when useful. Review the retrieved history against the conservator’s chosen limit for the particular objects. The resulting comparison can guide cabinet maintenance and storage allocation alongside object-condition inspections and the conservator’s material-specific storage plan.
applications.measurement: Record cabinet air relative humidity and temperature. Review sustained humidity departures and changes after servicing against criteria selected for the specific metals and contamination history.
applications.monitoringPoint: Choose an accessible air space inside the metal-storage cabinet, clear of desiccant and objects. Add a nearby room reference to distinguish enclosure behavior from room conditions.
applications.installation: Use a conservator-approved support and secure the logger against accidental movement. Keep its sensing area unobstructed and document retrieval procedures that minimize cabinet opening time.
applications.projectBrief: State the object types, cabinet design, conservator’s humidity criteria and servicing schedule. Confirm the required measurement conditions, logger positions, data collection duration and local PC review responsibilities.

applications.title: Photographic Collection Rooms
applications.description: Photographic collections contain different processes and supports, so a room history is more useful when linked to the actual holdings. Log air beside representative storage boxes and note retrieval or acclimatization periods. After downloading, compare conditions across room locations and operating seasons to support a preservation review. Where cooled storage is involved, confirm the logger configuration and allowable conditions before deployment and keep the study focused on air measurements.
applications.measurement: Measure storage air temperature and relative humidity for the relevant photographic materials. Compare long-term room behavior and handling periods with collection-specific preservation objectives.
applications.monitoringPoint: Select positions near representative shelving and the access area, without placing the sensor against boxes. Treat any separate acclimatization space as a distinct identified location.
applications.installation: Install on a secure shelf support outside photographic enclosures. Confirm environmental suitability for any cooled room and maintain a position register through every retrieval cycle.
applications.projectBrief: Describe photographic processes, enclosure types, room conditions and access routines. Supply the study period, available calibration requirements, chosen recording interval and a download plan for each location.

applications.title: Wooden Objects & Musical Instruments
applications.description: Wooden furniture and musical instruments can experience different air conditions in a store, rehearsal room or display area. Build a temperature and humidity history at the locations used for storage and handling, then review it after retrieval with the conservator’s notes. The records show when the surrounding environment changes, helping the team review room allocation and acclimatization practices alongside object inspections and the conservator’s material-specific handling guidance.
applications.measurement: Log air temperature and relative humidity during storage and handling. Assess the size and duration of changes using the conservator’s criteria for the particular wooden collection.
applications.monitoringPoint: Choose storage-height positions near the objects and a separate handling-space reference. Avoid radiator influence, direct sunlight and placement against the object or its protective case.
applications.installation: Secure the logger to independent furniture or an approved hanging point. Leave air clearance, record position and height, and coordinate retrieval with normal collection access.

Use several identified loggers to establish a time-based picture through occupied hours, weekends and seasonal changes. Retrieve their records on a planned route and compare locations in local PC software. The evidence helps archivists prioritize storage improvements and assess changes to ventilation or room use alongside an inspection of boxes and building conditions.
applications.measurement: Record air temperature and relative humidity at representative stack positions. Compare recurring daily patterns, seasonal drift and persistent differences between locations using archive-specific preservation criteria.
applications.monitoringPoint: Include upper and lower shelf levels, interior aisles and a perimeter area. Position sensors close to stored records but with enough clearance to represent surrounding air.
applications.installation: Use secure shelf mounts that remain accessible without moving archive boxes. Maintain a logger ID, aisle, bay and height register, supported by a location photograph.

applications.title: Rare Book Vaults

Log representative storage air over a full operating cycle and note door openings, maintenance and unusual occupancy. After scheduled retrieval, use the records to review the consistency of the vault environment and any persistent shelf differences. Pair this environmental evidence with the condition and enclosure needs of the books when selecting preservation actions.
applications.measurement: Measure vault air temperature and relative humidity continuously at the selected interval. Review variation and sustained departures against objectives established for the books and bindings.
applications.monitoringPoint: Choose representative book-storage heights and a position toward the vault perimeter. Keep the sensor clear of shelves, volumes and the immediate path of conditioned supply air.
applications.installation: Fix each logger on a stable, unobtrusive support approved by library staff. Document device ID and shelf location, then coordinate data retrieval with the vault access procedure.
